lit.str: The module exposes a pure solve(data) function in solution.py that accepts a JSON value and returns a JSON-serializable value.
declares required module and function interface
specifies input and output value domains
A callable solve(data) is defined in solution.py
The function accepts JSON-compatible input and returns a JSON-serializable value
Input has the structure {lines: [strings], operations: [{at, remove: [strings], insert: [strings]}].
declares input fields and their value types
Input contains lines and operations in the specified shapes
Each operation's at field denotes an integer boundary in the current line array.
The at boundary is interpreted against the current array
Apply each operation in order to a private copy of the input line array, using the current array produced by earlier successful operations.
specifies operation order and private working state
Changes for later operations are based on earlier successful operations
The input line array is not mutated
The solve function is deterministic for a given input.
Repeated calls with the same input produce the same JSON-serializable result
The public examples produce their specified outputs.
If at is outside the inclusive range from zero through the current array length, or at is a boolean, return {error:'range',operation:index} for that operation.
defines range validation and error result
Out-of-range at returns the range error with the current operation index
Boolean at returns the range error even though booleans are integer subclasses in Python
For an in-range boundary, require the entire remove sequence to match current lines beginning at at; a mismatch or a removal extending past EOF returns {error:'context',operation:index}.
defines context mismatch and overrun error
All removed strings match the corresponding current lines in order
A mismatch returns the context error with the current operation index
A removal extending past EOF returns the context error with the current operation index
After a successful context check, replace the matched sequence with insert.
The matched remove sequence is replaced by insert in the current line array
Unmatched lines retain their relative order
An empty remove sequence performs an insertion at at without removing lines; at equal to the current length permits appending.
specifies insertion behavior for empty context
empty remove operations and end boundary
Empty remove inserts all insert strings at the boundary
At equal to current length can append
On the first failed operation, return only its error result and do not publish any partial lines.
specifies failure stopping and transactional output
Processing stops at the first failure
Failure result contains only error and operation fields
No partially edited lines are returned
If every operation succeeds, return {lines: [strings]} containing the final line array in order.
Success result has the lines field with the final array
Line order is preserved as specified
Treat each line as an opaque string, including empty strings and strings containing newline characters.
Empty strings are preserved as line values
Embedded newline characters are not used to split or normalize strings
The implementation uses only the Python standard library and performs no external I/O.
No non-standard library dependency is required
